persona: Screen-print production designer, 25 years preparing art for one-colour screen printing on tees: dot size and dot gain at print size, shadows filling in, highlights dropping out, ink load, how the halftone looks on cotton.

designs.title: Oak and Fox Earth
designs.why: Same tree, same soil, same halftone issues, but the den is bigger and fills its pocket: a vixen with four cubs tucked against her, with clear faces and ears. It reads as the focal point from across a room, and the light fur against the dark den gives the one real high-contrast moment in the lower half. The cluster is a little crowded (the bodies of the right-hand cub and the vixen merge), and the trunk shadow and twig dot-chains still have the press problems of version 1. The soil fade-out ends in a slightly hard, ragged line of minimum dots at the bottom edge. Printable and sellable, not yet catalogue-best.
designs.fix: Lighten the soil midtones so the roots read dark on light like the crown on the sky, and cap the den interior and trunk shadow at about 65% to allow for gain on cotton. That one tonal pass would lift the whole lower half.
